standard_prerequisites.name: Injection and surjection
standard_prerequisites.statement: f : A -> B is injective when its fibers are mere propositions, and surjective when every fiber is merely inhabited.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both notions are the subject of the three implications.

standard_prerequisites.name: Excluded middle
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every proposition P, P or not P.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is assumed for the whole statement and used at source line 825 to decide a fiber.

standard_prerequisites.name: Axiom of choice
standard_prerequisites.statement: A surjection merely has a section.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is assumed in the third part and used at source line 830.

core_obligations: First part: given an injection f and a point a_0 : A, define g : B -> A by cases; since f is injective its fibers are mere propositions, so by excluded middle one may decide whether a fiber is inhabited, and one sets g(b) to a witness when it is and to a_0 otherwise (source lines 823-826).
Show that a = g(f(a)) for all a, so that g is surjective (source line 827).
Second part: conclude that if A is merely inhabited then an injection gives a merely existing surjection, by induction on the truncation (source line 829).
Third part: assuming the axiom of choice, a surjection g gives a merely existing function f : A -> B with g(f(a)) = a for all a, and any such f is injective (source lines 830-831).

proof_roadmap.step: From an injection build a surjection by a case distinction using excluded middle.
Derive the truncated statement by induction on truncation.
From a surjection build an injection using the axiom of choice.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.2.9 at source lines 805-821: assuming excluded middle, an injection between cardinalities yields a surjection given a point of the source, hence a merely existing surjection when the source is merely inhabited, and assuming the axiom of choice a surjection yields a merely existing injection. The author's proof (source lines 822-832) has three parts that use different hypotheses: the first builds the surjection by a case distinction on whether a fiber is inhabited, which is legitimate precisely because injectivity makes the fibers mere propositions and excluded middle decides them (lines 823-826); the second is an induction on truncation (line 829); and the third extracts an injective map from a surjection by the axiom of choice and observes that any section of a surjection is injective (lines 830-831). The statement records the three implications and never says that the case distinction in the first part is where contradiction-freedom of the fibers is consumed.
